result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions due to its support pillars. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and a marked crosswalk exist, the faded markings and lack of daylighting at the intersection increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Structural Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large steel pillars for the elevated train structure block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line on both sides of the street.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to motorists.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the intersection further obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to move pedestrians past the pillars and parked cars, improving visibility and shortening crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection located under an elevated structure, featuring marked continental crosswalks and sidewalks. While basic infrastructure like traffic signals and curb ramps are present, the wide roadway and potential sightline obstructions from the overhead pillars increase pedestrian exposure and risk.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Geometry
hazards.description: The open geometry of the intersection increases pedestrian exposure time and may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Pillars from the overhead structure can create blind spots, blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and left side of the image

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised refuge island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages and provide a physical barrier.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a two-lane street situated beneath an elevated rail structure, which creates significant visual obstructions due to large support pillars. While sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the shadows and physical barriers from the overhead infrastructure reduce visibility and safety at the crossing.

hazards.name: Elevated Structure Pillars
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated rail line are positioned near the curb, significantly blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway, flanking the travel lanes.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection further obscure the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the pillars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse markings to a ladder or zebra pattern to increase the visibility of the crossing zone.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals within a mixed-use urban setting. While basic infrastructure is present, the lack of curb extensions and the presence of parked vehicles near the crossing points create potential visibility issues.

hazards.name: Restricted Sightlines
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on both sides of the street near the intersection reduce visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs adjacent to the crosswalks on both sides of the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Protection
hazards.description: The absence of curb extensions or bollards at the corners increases the exposure of pedestrians to turning traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection.
